title: Online Study on the Impact of a Self-Help Tool for Social Anxiety
official: Online Study on the Impact of a Self-Help Tool for Social Anxiety
summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to understand which individuals benefit most from an internet-based cognitive behavioral intervention for social anxiety. Adults aged 18-65 will complete a self-guided online program designed to reduce anxiety symptoms. The investigators will use a combination of self-reported clinical information and data from computerized decision-making and cognitive tasks to predict behavioral change due to the intervention.

interventions.name: Internet-delivered self-help for social anxiety based on principles of cognitive behavioral therapy

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 to 65 years
* Live in the United States
* Comfortable reading and writing in English
* Have regular access to the internet and a desktop/laptop computer
* Report wanting to feel more comfortable in social situations, to improve social confidence, and/or to reduce symptoms of social anxiety as primary reason for joining the study
* Have a valid photo ID and be willing to complete a video-based identity verification call if requested

Exclusion Criteria:

* Lack of attention when completing parts of the study, and/or not completing the study tasks as instructed

sites.f: Princeton University, but recruitment and study are conducted completely online and can occur anywhere in the US.
